title: Easy and Difficult
label: ch:ml-ease
canDo: I can say that something is easy or difficult.

payoff.summary: From cold: the pair, and the welding of a word ending in anusvara onto aaNu, which the learner has been performing since near the beginning without being shown it.
payoff.note: TWO atoms and NO NEW GRAMMAR. eLuppam + aaNu -> eLuppamaaNu is not a new rule: sukhamaaNu is attested from chapter 3, ishtamaaNu from 34, kudumbamaaNu from 35 and moshamaaNu from 89. CORRECTED IN REVIEW: an earlier draft said nobody had ever pointed the join out, which is FALSE -- ML-C89-mosham states it outright and TESTS it in its own Wrap-up Recall, seven chapters before this one, in the lesson that gives the learner moshanam itself. The chapter now says it was named once, at moshaM, and that here it stops being a fact about one given word and becomes something the learner does. The MECHANISM was corrected too: the anusvara does not 'turn into' ma as a sound change -- it already IS the sound m, and only the writing changes, because aaNu puts a vowel behind it and the bare sign cannot carry one. Saying the two words in a row, nothing is heard to change, which is exactly why the learner has been doing it unnoticed. buddhimuttu was considered for a third lesson and dropped rather than assert register nuances that could not be defended.
